newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 19.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

According to News Ltd executive director of sport Ian Frykberg, Rupert Murdoch plans to keep funding the Super League competition for as long as it takes to establish that it is No.1. Peace talks with the ARL were cancelled after Super League objected to Optus Vision's previously undiscussed demands. Page 20.

AFL's Collingwood player Nathan Buckley is still eligible for the Brownlow Medal after being cleared by the Tribunal of kneeing Essendon's Barry Young. Collingwood team mate Damian Monkhorst's season was ended however, when he pleaded guilty to striking, and was suspended for three weeks. Page 20.

Australian motorcyclist Michael Doohan has defeated his Japanese team mate, Tadayuki Okada, in the British Grand Prix to win his fourth consecutive 500cc motorcycling world championship. Thirty-thousand spectators were at Donington Park to witness yet anther benchmark in Doohan's career. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

ARL North Sydney Bears prop Josh Stuart will miss the next three games, including the team's first semi-final, after being found guilty last night of a reckless high tackle. Club chief executive Bob Saunders found the judiciary's decision disappointing. Page 42

Australian Cricket chairman of selectors Trevor Hohns said Australia's Test captain should no longer be guaranteed the job of leading the country's limited-over side. Hohns has called a provision allowing a specialist captain to take the team for one-day matches when necessary. Page 40.

In AFL, the Sydney Swans injury list has shortened since Sunday with only forward Mark Bayes a definite non-starter for next Saturday's match against Carlton. To guarantee the Swans a home ground final they need to win this weekend's match. Page 41.
THE AGE

The Building Controls Commission has cleared AFL's Western Bulldogs to play at the Whitten Oval for the last time on Saturday. Major work needs to be done on the ground and no games will be played on it for the next year. Page B10.

Tennis player Patrick Rafter has moved to number 14 in the world after defeating Yevgeny Kafelnikov. Rafter survived three set matches in a row on his way to his fourth ATP final of the year. Page B9.

Cricketer Steve Waugh's right thumb is causing him pain after he bruised it making his double centuries at Old Trafford. The acting captain made his fourth century of the tour, leading Australia to victory against Kent. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

AFL North Melbourne star Anthony Rock has been cleared of a serious knee injury. Rock injured the knee in North's loss to Richmond on Sunday, and will face a fitness test before playing against Hawthorn this weekend. Page 78.

Australian golfer Karrie Webb won the British Open women's golf title on Sunday, finishing the final round with an eight-shot lead. Karrie's win comes after her last-round meltdown at the Ladies Masters earlier in the year. Page 74.

Golfer Greg Norman finshed equal 13th yesterday in the USA PGA golf championship, bringing his eleven year streak to an end. Norman finished outside the top 10 in all four major golf championships for the first time since 1985. Page 75.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Socceroo coach Terry Venables has issued a challenge to England to play Australia at Wembley in the event that both teams qualify for next year's World Cup in France. Venables said he was eager for a clash with his English successor Glen Hodle. Page 66.

Rugby Union Wallaby captain John Eales yesterday signed a new three-year contract with the Australin Rugby Union, believed to be worth about A$1.8 million over the next four years. Eales s still recovering from a medial ligament problem. Page 66.

In golf, Davis Love III won the USA PGA Championship by five strokes to edge out British Open Champion Justin Leonard. Love dedicated the win to his father who showed him how to play golf at an early age. Page 63
